sections.title: Quantities that still disagree
sections.intro: Rebuilt after the workbook's formula faults were fixed. Every line is now compared on the basis its own formula points at — raw against raw, cooked against cooked — so unit mismatches no longer show up as differences. 44 of the 56 comparable lines agree and are not listed. Nine rows that appeared here earlier have been withdrawn: they were never differences, they were an error in how the comparison read the sheet. Korean Spicy Beef was one of them — sheet and app both say 4.2.

sections.title: Recipe links to confirm
sections.intro: Ingredient lines that never connected to the recipe that makes them — the same fault as the Lentils one. Until linked, everything below reads zero. Confirm whether the proposed recipe is right.

sections.title: Ingredients that point at themselves
sections.intro: The importer matched by name, so these recipes list themselves as their own ingredient. Ordering totals are already corrected in the app; the data still needs cleaning. “Raw purchase” means bought in, not made here.

sections.title: Discontinued or still made?
sections.intro: Down to 5 dishes and 6 meals. Every one of these is absent from the production workbook entirely — the sheet has already dropped them — so they are almost certainly discontinued and only trickling in from long-standing customers. Confirm and they can be closed. The pre-production items that were here (egg bites, oats, truffles, the Portions products) have all been linked and are gone from this list.

sections.title: Ingredient names counted twice
sections.intro: The same ingredient is spelled several ways, so the raw-materials total splits across them. Harmless on a cook sheet, dangerous on a picking or ordering list. Confirm each group really is one item.

sections.title: Decisions — James
sections.intro: These change how the app behaves rather than what the data says.

items.title: Dry-goods picking sheet
items.evidence: The convention is settled: component recipes are DRY weight, finished and meal recipes are COOKED. The app already totals every dry ingredient in the Raw materials list, and after the self-link fix it now matches your sheet almost exactly — Penne 4.06 vs 4.06, Fusilli 2.09 vs 2.09, Gnocchi 2.88 vs 2.88. What is missing is a picking sheet: that same list grouped by where it is stored and printable, so the team knows what dry pasta and grain to pull for the day. Where should it live — its own tab, or a section of Production needs?

items.title: Ingredient names need merging before the picking sheet is usable
items.evidence: The raw-materials total is split across spellings of the same ingredient: Salt (2.76) and SALT (0.01); Coconut Milk (2.97) and Coconut milk (2.12); Garlic IQF across three spellings. Fifteen groups in all. For a picking or ordering list this is dangerous — you would pull twice or miss some entirely. Merging them is straightforward once someone confirms each pair really is the same item.

items.title: Long-tail orders for discontinued dishes
items.evidence: Dishes that are off the menu still receive occasional orders from long-standing customers — Jerk Chicken, Seafood Chowder, Lamb and Apricot Kofta among them. They arrive on the production list, get packed, but have no components, so the kitchen gets no requirement for them. James has flagged that how the website handles these needs addressing separately. Logged here so it is not lost; not for this pass.

items.title: Simmer top-ups are not imported
items.evidence: The dish import takes the D2C column only and matches exactly at 1,365 meals. The workbook's 1,377 includes 6 Simmer on SKU 6 and 6 on SKU 65. Should the importer add Simmer to the same SKU, or keep the wholesale lane separate?

items.title: Protect the workbook's formula cells
items.evidence: Four cells had a number typed over the formula: Thai Green Curry (40.96 vs 6.03 correct), Pearl Barley (8.0 vs 4.07), Tagine Couscous (4.7 vs 3.10), Pickled Chilli (1.0 vs 0.46). Every one overstated production. All four are patched. Worth protecting those cells in the Google Sheet so it cannot happen again.

items.title: Build the component editor
items.evidence: Every remaining item on this board is someone needing to change data they cannot currently touch — link an ingredient, merge two names, add components to a dish. There is no screen in the app that adds, renames or retires a component, so all of it routes through Claude. That is also how three names for one chicken came about: someone needed a line for chopped chicken, had no way to add one, and typed a new name into the sheet. A small editor turns the last stretch of this from a bottleneck into work the team can just do.
